summary: Unexpected 5xx layered failures during load-shed reassignment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed a sustained elevated 5xx error rate (~8-12% of requests) for the NovaCRM account starting 2026-03-13 22:10 UTC. Errors manifest as a mixture of 502 and 504 responses from the API Gateway, and multiple upstream runtime SIGTERM/restart events. The issue surfaced after an automated load-shedding reassignment job ran for tenant weight rebalancing.

Impact:
- NovaCRM reported degraded application performance and partial feature outages for their end users (churn risk).
- Error rate elevated for all chat and embedding routes for the committed dedicated pool.
- Multiple customer requests timed out or returned 5xx for ~55 minutes before mitigation steps.

Environment:
- prod: us-east (dedicated gpu pool cluster r-w-12)
- Route types: streaming chat (long-lived), non-streaming text generation, embeddings
- Models in-use: rw-inference-v2 pinned for the customer's dedicated pool

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Scheduled load-shed reassignment job initiated to redistribute tenant weights across ephemeral proxies and router groups.
2) Routing table updates started rolling; some proxy nodes received higher inbound fan-in during reassignment.
3) Keepalive pruning kicked in concurrently on a subset of proxies due to FD pressure.
4) Upstream runtimes serving the tenant logged repeated preemption and SIGTERM as their worker pools attempted to gracefully drain.
5) The API Gateway returned 502/504 to customers when proxy handoffs timed out or connections were reset.

Logs and metrics collected:
- api-gateway access logs: surge in 502/504 from 22:10–23:05 UTC (sample attached in ticket).
- proxy metrics: AcceptQueueDepth spiked from 12 -> 156 on two proxies, FD_use 92%.
- runtime logs: repeated "Received SIGTERM for graceful shutdown" followed by "Worker exit: code 137" around 22:18 UTC.
- scheduler events: reassignment job started 22:05, completed 22:40 with several retries on node-bind failures.
- Observed KV cache evictions increase and backend latency (p95 token latency) rising from 120ms -> 420ms during the window.

Initial mitigation performed by Support/SRE:
- Paused ongoing reassignment sweep at 22:28 UTC.
- Manually rebalanced a subset of heavy routes away from saturated proxies at 22:35 UTC.
- Increased keepalive window temporarily to reduce pruning by 22:42 UTC.
Result: error rate decreased to baseline over ~20 minutes.

2026-03-13 22:30 UTC - SRE (Ethan Patel): Observed accept-queue spike and FD pressure on proxy-7 and proxy-9. Paused reassignment job. Requesting routing table snapshot and runtime core dumps.

2026-03-14 09:10 UTC - Support (Mariana Lopez): Follow-up email to customer with incident summary and interim mitigations. Awaiting confirmation on whether additional rollouts impacted other tenants.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: (1) The reassignment algorithm momentarily concentrated high-weight streaming routes on proxies with stale keepalive state, amplifying FD pressure and triggering pruning. (2) Runtime preemption logic is too aggressive when signaled by proxy-side connection resets, leading to worker exit instead of graceful drain. Evidence: accept-queue spikes align with reassignment windows; runtimes show SIGTERM + OOM-ish exits (exit code 137) consistent with degraded host resources. Next checks: full thread and heap profiles from runtimes during the window; router table diffs pre- and post-reassignment; check kernel-level closed socket counts and ulimit settings on affected proxies.
resolution:
Short-term: Paused reassignment sweep during high-traffic windows and increased keepalive thresholds to avoid mass pruning. Implemented manual route smoothing to distribute heavy streams across healthy proxies.
Medium-term: Engineering to adjust reassignment throttle to consider live accept-queue depth and FD utilization metrics before moving weights. Plan to update runtime shutdown handling to wait longer for active streaming sessions and avoid premature SIGTERM escalation.
Follow-ups: Create an INT ticket to add a pre-flight check to the reassignment controller (INT-4051). Schedule a postmortem runbook for dedicated pool rebalances and update customer-facing guidance for maintenance windows. Target ETA for medium-term changes: 2026-04-02.
next_steps: ENG: Implement pre-flight health gating for reassignment controller (linked INT-4051).
SRE: Add alert for AcceptQueueDepth > 100 sustained for 2m on any proxy (owner: SRE-routing).
DX: Notify affected customers about revised maintenance windows and provide mitigation guidance.
Postmortem: Owner assigned to Mariana Lopez, due 2026-03-20.
